title: Allocate Time in Each Day for Both Strategic and Tactical Work
author: Admired Leadership
summary: Opening with Peter Drucker's distinction between "doing things right" and "doing the right things," this article argues that daily execution routinely crowds out strategic thinking unless leaders deliberately protect time for it. It observes that most leaders reserve big-picture thinking for occasional off-sites and planning days, which the author says is insufficient, strategic attention needs to be a daily habit, not an occasional event. The piece recommends spending an hour or more each day on longer-term issues like market trends, growth opportunities, and resource allocation, plus regular conversations with a range of people specifically to escape conventional thinking. It closes by framing balance between detail-orientation and big-picture vision as the daily discipline that separates effective leaders from merely busy ones.
points: Day-to-day execution reliably crowds out strategic thinking unless leaders deliberately protect time for it every day, not just at off-sites.
The best leaders reserve an hour or more daily for market trends, growth opportunities, policy formulation, and resource-allocation thinking.
Talking to a range of people regularly is framed as an escape hatch from "task-myopia" and conventional thinking, not just an information source.
Spending time on big-picture thinking daily also signals to the team that planning is essential to execution, not separate from it.
quotes: In his attempt to emphasize the difference between efficiency and effectiveness, management guru Peter Drucker famously drew a line between “doing things right” and “doing the right things.
The problem is that leaders are commonly pulled away from thinking long-term.
They know that without giving time to strategic issues every day, they lose sight of the big picture and risk doing the wrong things.
They know that task-myopia can blind them to the realities that influence their long-term success.
Spending an hour or more every day on bigger-picture thinking not only ensures effectiveness, but it also shows the team that planning is essential for excellence in execution.
